The inequality **holds**. Below is the proof.

**Claim.** For any positive definite matrices $\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Y} \succ 0$ and any $\lambda \in (0,1)$,
$$
(1-\lambda)\mathbf{X}^{-1}+\lambda\mathbf{Y}^{-1} \;\succeq\; \bigl((1-\lambda)\mathbf{X}+\lambda\mathbf{Y}\bigr)^{-1}.
$$

**Proof.** Define the matrix-valued function
$$
h(t) \;=\; \bigl(\mathbf{X}+t(\mathbf{Y}-\mathbf{X})\bigr)^{-1}, \qquad t\in[0,1].
$$
Set $\mathbf{D}=\mathbf{Y}-\mathbf{X}$ and $\mathbf{M}(t)=\mathbf{X}+t\mathbf{D}$. Since $\mathbf{M}(t)=(1-t)\mathbf{X}+t\mathbf{Y}$ is a convex combination of two positive definite matrices, $\mathbf{M}(t)\succ 0$ for every $t\in[0,1]$, so $h$ is well defined and smooth. Note $h(0)=\mathbf{X}^{-1}$, $h(1)=\mathbf{Y}^{-1}$, and $h(\lambda)=\bigl((1-\lambda)\mathbf{X}+\lambda\mathbf{Y}\bigr)^{-1}$.

Differentiating (using $\frac{d}{dt}\mathbf{M}^{-1}=-\mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{M}'\mathbf{M}^{-1}$):
$$
h'(t)=-\mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{D}\,\mathbf{M}^{-1},
$$
$$
h''(t)=2\,\mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{D}\,\mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{D}\,\mathbf{M}^{-1}.
$$

Let $\mathbf{C}=\mathbf{M}^{-1/2}\mathbf{D}\,\mathbf{M}^{-1/2}$, which is symmetric. Substituting $\mathbf{D}=\mathbf{M}^{1/2}\mathbf{C}\mathbf{M}^{1/2}$:
$$
\mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{D}\,\mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{D}\,\mathbf{M}^{-1}
= \mathbf{M}^{-1/2}\mathbf{C}^{2}\mathbf{M}^{-1/2}.
$$
Hence
$$
h''(t)=2\,\mathbf{M}^{-1/2}\mathbf{C}^{2}\mathbf{M}^{-1/2}\;\succeq\;0,
$$
because $\mathbf{C}^{2}\succeq 0$ (it is a square of a symmetric matrix) and congruence by $\mathbf{M}^{-1/2}$ preserves the Loewner order. Thus $h''(t)\succeq 0$ for all $t\in[0,1]$.

Now use the integral form of the Taylor expansion. For any $\lambda\in(0,1)$:
$$
h(\lambda)=h(0)+\lambda h'(0)+\int_{0}^{\lambda}(\lambda-t)\,h''(t)\,dt,
$$
$$
(1-\lambda)h(0)+\lambda h(1)=h(0)+\lambda h'(0)+\lambda\int_{0}^{1}(1-t)\,h''(t)\,dt.
$$
Subtracting,
$$
(1-\lambda)h(0)+\lambda h(1)-h(\lambda)
=\int_{0}^{\lambda}t(1-\lambda)\,h''(t)\,dt+\int_{\lambda}^{1}\lambda(1-t)\,h''(t)\,dt.
$$
On $[0,\lambda]$ the scalar coefficient $t(1-\lambda)$ is non-negative; on $[\lambda,1]$ the coefficient $\lambda(1-t)$ is non-negative. Since $h''(t)\succeq 0$ throughout, each integrand is positive semi-definite, and so the integrals — being limits of PSD combinations — are PSD. Therefore
$$
(1-\lambda)h(0)+\lambda h(1)-h(\lambda)\;\succeq\;0.
$$
Recalling the values of $h$ at $0,1,\lambda$:
$$
(1-\lambda)\mathbf{X}^{-1}+\lambda\mathbf{Y}^{-1}\;\succeq\;\bigl((1-\lambda)\mathbf{X}+\lambda\mathbf{Y}\bigr)^{-1}.
$$

This establishes the inequality for all positive definite $\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y}$ and all $\lambda\in(0,1)$. (Equivalently, the matrix inverse map is *operator convex* on the cone of positive definite matrices.) $\blacksquare$
